english: (particle) signaling shared or obvious knowledge
note: as a Modalpartikel (not the plain "yes"), ja signals that something should already be obvious or known — often with surprise or enthusiasm.

examples.en: That's great! (I'm pleasantly surprised / you can see that too, right?)

english: (particle) insisting, reminding, or softening an imperative
note: one of the most versatile Modalpartikeln — in a statement it reminds ("you know that"), in a command it encourages ("go on, do it").

examples.en: Come on, join us!

english: (particle) that's just how it is — resignation
note: expresses that a fact simply can't be changed — a slightly more neutral, standard-German alternative to halt.

examples.en: That's just the way it is.

english: (particle) that's just how it is — colloquial resignation
note: the same resigned sense as eben, but more colloquial and regionally marked (especially southern Germany, Austria).

examples.de: Man kann halt nicht alles haben.
examples.en: You just can't have everything.

english: (particle) reassuring permission in an imperative
note: in an imperative, ruhig reassures the listener that an action is fine — no need to hesitate or ask.

examples.de: Frag ruhig, wenn du etwas nicht verstehst.
examples.en: Feel free to ask if there's something you don't understand.

english: (particle) reassurance, confidence that things will work out
note: as a Modalpartikel, schon reassures — a completely different job from its literal meaning "already" (bereits).

examples.en: It'll work out, don't worry.

english: (particle) urgency or warning
note: adds real urgency to a warning or wish — much stronger than the plain request without it.

examples.en: Whatever you do, don't do that!

english: (particle) urgency, especially in wishes
note: close to bloß in urgent wishes and warnings — "wenn ich das nur gewusst hätte" = "if only I'd known."

examples.de: Wenn ich das nur gewusst hätte!
examples.en: If only I had known that!

english: (particle) softening a request, casualness
note: makes an imperative or request sound more casual and less demanding — very common in everyday speech.

examples.en: Can you help me for a sec?

english: (particle) genuine curiosity or mild surprise in a question
note: a completely different word from the causal conjunction denn (B1 Unit 3, "because") — here it adds interest to a question.

examples.en: What are you doing there? (I'm curious/a little surprised)

english: (particle) exclamatory surprise
note: in an exclamation, vielleicht doesn't mean "maybe" at all — it intensifies, similar to "what a …!"

examples.en: What a mess this is!

english: (particle) casual curiosity, mild topic shift
note: softens a question into something more casual — close to "by the way" — distinct from its literal sense "actually."

examples.en: What time is it, by the way?

english: That's great! — ja example
note: ja adds a note of "you can see that too" or pleasant surprise to a plain statement.

examples.en: That's great!

english: Come on, join us! — doch example
note: doch turns a bare command into a warm invitation.

examples.en: Come on, join us!

english: Yes I do! / Yes it is! — contradicting a negative statement or question
note: a distinct, standalone use of doch: the specific German word for contradicting a negative ("Du magst das nicht." — "Doch!").

examples.de: Du hast doch keine Zeit, oder? — Doch, ich habe Zeit!
examples.en: You don't have time, do you? — Yes I do!

english: That's just the way it is — eben example
note: a shrug in word form — nothing more can be said or done about it.

examples.en: That's just the way it is.

german: Man kann halt nicht alles haben
english: You just can't have everything — halt example
note: the colloquial twin of das ist eben so.

examples.de: Man kann halt nicht alles haben.
examples.en: You just can't have everything.

german: Frag ruhig, wenn du etwas nicht verstehst
english: Feel free to ask if there's something you don't understand — ruhig example
note: reassures the listener there's no downside to asking.

examples.de: Frag ruhig, wenn du etwas nicht verstehst.
examples.en: Feel free to ask if there's something you don't understand.

english: It'll work out, don't worry — schon example
note: a common, warm reassurance said to calm someone down.

examples.de: Mach dir keine Sorgen, das wird schon klappen.
examples.en: Don't worry, it'll work out.

english: Whatever you do, don't do that! — bloß example
note: a genuinely urgent warning, much stronger than "mach das nicht" alone.

examples.de: Mach das bloß nicht, das könnte gefährlich sein!
examples.en: Whatever you do, don't do that, it could be dangerous!

german: Wenn ich das nur gewusst hätte!
english: If only I had known that! — nur example
note: an urgent wish about the past — nur intensifies the regret.

examples.de: Wenn ich das nur gewusst hätte!
examples.en: If only I had known that!

english: Can you help me for a sec? — mal example
note: mal makes the request sound casual and low-effort, not demanding.

examples.en: Can you help me for a sec?

english: What are you doing there? — denn example
note: denn adds curiosity or mild surprise — a flat "Was machst du da?" would sound almost interrogative by comparison.

examples.en: What are you doing there?

english: What a mess this is! — vielleicht example
note: an exclamatory use, not a statement of uncertainty — context and intonation make the difference clear.

examples.en: What a mess this is!

english: What time is it, by the way? — eigentlich example
note: eigentlich here signals a casual, half-related question, not "what is the actual time as opposed to the apparent one."

examples.en: What time is it, by the way?

english: a usage contrast: reassurance vs. the literal meaning "already"
note: "Ich bin schon fertig" (I'm already done) is literal; "Das wird schon" (it'll be fine) is the Modalpartikel — same word, unrelated job.

examples.de: Ich bin schon fertig. / Das wird schon.
examples.en: I'm already done. / It'll be fine.

english: a usage contrast: a curiosity particle in questions vs. the causal conjunction "because"
note: "Was machst du denn?" (curiosity) has nothing to do with "Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn es regnet" (B1 Unit 3's causal denn) — same spelling, unrelated grammar.

examples.de: Was machst du denn? / Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn es regnet.
examples.en: What are you up to? / I'm staying home, because it's raining.

german: Modalpartikeln ändern die Einstellung, nicht die Bedeutung
english: modal particles change the attitude, not the propositional meaning
note: removing a Modalpartikel never makes a sentence factually wrong — it just makes it sound flatter, more like a textbook and less like a real person talking.

examples.de: Komm mit! vs. Komm doch mal mit!
examples.en: Come along! vs. Come on, why don't you come along!
